| [CASE-337](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-337.md) | Beta–Bernoulli features vs shared-driver null | [LEAD-144](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-144.md)'s study, the "Option A" [CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md) recommends, in one linear family. Twenty-four members in six overlapping working groups, with a communication graph built from the groups, are simulated in three worlds: coupled along the graph; driven by one persistent external driver per group with no interaction; and half of each. The driver's gain is tuned so that every world shows the same within-group correlation, 0.30. CASE-165's finite beta-Bernoulli model (K = 16, α = 3) and four comparators are fitted to 600 days of each world and scored on interventions none was fitted to: a pulse to a member, and the cut of a group's internal ties. Over seven organizations, the feature model finds more features under the null (11.1) than under coupling (8.7), better aligned with the groups (Jaccard 0.72 against 0.44); read as causes of members it is exact under the driver and misses every cut under coupling, and read as realized by its holders it is wrong in both. The communication graph alone is right under coupling and invents coupling under the driver (a predicted cut effect of −0.18 where the truth is 0); the features added to it leave that error (0.21), and observing the true driver removes it (0.006). One-step fit ranks the models the same way in every world. The design, code and wording are the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-362](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-362.md) v2 | Shared perspective in five trained populations | [CASE-145](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-145.md) run as [LEAD-087](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-087.md) asked, after its criterion was stated. Thirty simulated members learn six category prototypes from one structured schema; at test they meet in pairs on stimuli from a shared world, with sparse feedback from it matched across arms. Five interaction arms: none (correlated responses), conformity during training only (socially learned norms), unconditional conformity, enforcement by a referee, and disagreements checked against the world. Each also ran with and without a vote that enacts a collective action and learns from a collective reward. Some members' interpretation of one category was perturbed, with the world moving the same way (warranted) or not. Over 20 seeds, every population is structurally concordant, and only the interacting ones draw the perturbed members back; but unperturbed members take up at most 2% of the deviation, under the 5% stated in advance, so none passes cross-member dependence and none shares a perspective by either reading. The evidential condition ranks the arms as predicted (0.025 against 0.004 for conformity) below its stated 0.05, in five settings. Conformity passes the restorative condition, which therefore fails A4's test. The vote gives collective agency in every arm and its absence none, so the study gives no constructed instance of perspective without collective agency. A stipulated model, one size. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
